application.stem: A tracker reports x(t)=4t metres and y(t)=10-2t^2 metres for one particle in one fixed frame. Find the particle's position at t=2 s, and explain why x(2 s) may not be paired with y(3 s) to describe one position.
conditions: The two functions refer to the same particle and the same time coordinate.
Use the declared fixed x-y frame.

reasoning_route.action: Treat x(t) and y(t) as two coordinate projections of the same particle in one fixed frame, tied to one common event time t.
reasoning_route.why_valid: A single plane position is defined by simultaneous coordinates of one particle; independent component functions do not create independent clocks.
reasoning_route.output: Both coordinates must be evaluated at the same t before they can form one position.

reasoning_route.action: Substitute t=2 s into both component functions to obtain x(2)=8 m and y(2)=2 m.
reasoning_route.why_valid: The requested state is the event labelled t=2 s, so both component functions must be sampled at that event.
reasoning_route.output: The simultaneous coordinate values are x=8 m and y=2 m.

reasoning_route.action: Pair the two simultaneous values as the position (8,2) m and reject x(2) paired with y(3) as a single physical state.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Coordinates form one state only when they refer to the same object, frame and instant; changing one timestamp changes the event.
reasoning_route.output: The valid t=2 s position is (8,2) m; x(2),y(3) is not one position.

reasoning_route.action: Attach the timestamp to each component value and confirm the two timestamps match before calling the pair a position.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Timestamp agreement is an independent event-identity check that does not depend on the arithmetic values themselves.
reasoning_route.output: Both values carry t=2 s, so the reconstructed state is temporally consistent.

hints.text: What must be the same when x(t) and y(t) describe one particle at one instant?
Evaluate both component functions at the requested t before pairing them.

scaffolds.text: Write x(t) and y(t) in two columns connected to one clock t before substituting any number.
Label the time beside each evaluated component before you pair the coordinates.

application.check: The answer must use one t for both components; mixing timestamps produces no real single-time state.

solution.summary: At t=2 s, x=8 m and y=2 m, so the position is (8,2) m in the declared frame. x(2 s) and y(3 s) cannot form one position because they refer to different instants.
steps: Evaluate both component descriptions at the same requested time.
A physical plane state is a simultaneous component pair.

repair.action: Recombine only component values that refer to the same frame and the same instant.
repair.why_valid: Mixing x at one time with y at another does not describe any single physical state of the object.
repair.output: one physically valid plane state reconstructed from simultaneous components
